   "source": [
    "# ARIMA: Time Series Forecasting\n",
    "\n",
    "[![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/tatsuki-washimi/gwexpy/blob/main/docs/web/en/user_guide/tutorials/advanced_arima.ipynb)\n",
    "\n",
    "This notebook demonstrates how to model and forecast time series data using ARIMA-related functions (AR, MA, ARMA, ARIMA/SARIMAX) that have been added to the `gwexpy` `TimeSeries` class.\n",
    "\n",
    "- **Related API**: [Time Series API](../../reference/api/timeseries.rst)\n",
    "- **Related theory**: [Validated Algorithms](../validated_algorithms.md), [Numerical Stability](../numerical_stability.md)\n",
    "\n",
    "## Setup\n",
    "\n",
    "Import the necessary libraries."
   ]
  },

   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "0bc86dfd",
   "metadata": {

   "source": [
    "import warnings\n",
    "\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import sklearn.utils.validation\n",
    "\n",
    "# Monkeypatch for pmdarima compatibility with scikit-learn >= 1.6\n",
    "_orig_check_array = sklearn.utils.validation.check_array\n",
    "\n",
    "def _patched_check_array(*args, **kwargs):\n",
    "    kwargs.pop(\"force_all_finite\", None)\n",
    "    return _orig_check_array(*args, **kwargs)\n",
    "\n",
    "sklearn.utils.validation.check_array = _patched_check_array\n",
    "\n",
    "warnings.filterwarnings(\n",
    "    \"ignore\", message=r\".*force_all_finite.*\", category=FutureWarning\n",
    ")\n",
    "warnings.filterwarnings(\"ignore\", category=FutureWarning, module=r\"sklearn\\..*\")\n",
    "warnings.filterwarnings(\"ignore\", category=FutureWarning, module=r\"pmdarima\\..*\")\n",
    "\n",
    "from gwexpy.timeseries import TimeSeries"
   ]
  },
  {

   "id": "435a1808",
   "metadata": {

   "source": [
    "## Creating Sample Data\n",
    "\n",
    "To verify the effectiveness of ARIMA models, we create synthetic data that includes a trend, seasonality (periodicity), and noise."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "7b176c91",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-07-03T16:52:34.282572Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-07-03T16:52:34.282102Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-07-03T16:52:49.737822Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-07-03T16:52:49.736823Z"
    },
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 15.476503,
     "end_time": "2026-07-03T16:52:49.739295+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-07-03T16:52:34.262792+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Plot size 1200x600 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# Trend + Seasonality + Noise\n",
    "t0 = 0\n",
    "dt = 0.1\n",
    "duration = 30\n",
    "t = np.arange(0, duration, dt)\n",
    "n_samples = len(t)\n",
    "\n",
    "# 1. Linear Trend\n",
    "trend = 0.3 * t\n",
    "\n",
    "# 2. Periodic component (Sine)\n",
    "seasonality = 2.0 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 0.2 * t)\n",
    "\n",
    "# 3. Noise\n",
    "np.random.seed(42)\n",
    "noise = np.random.normal(0, 0.8, n_samples)\n",
    "\n",
    "data = trend + seasonality + noise\n",
    "\n",
    "# Create TimeSeries object\n",
    "ts = TimeSeries(data, t0=t0, dt=dt, unit=\"V\", name=\"Sample Data\")\n",
    "\n",
    "ts.plot()\n",
    "plt.title(\"Original Data (Trend + Seasonality + Noise)\")\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {

   "id": "bfc1fddd",
   "metadata": {

   "source": [
    "## 1. AR (AutoRegressive) Model\n",
    "\n",
    "The AR model assumes that the current value depends on past values.\n",
    "Use the `ts.ar(p)` method, where `p` is the order."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "af32da7a",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-07-03T16:52:49.786015Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-07-03T16:52:49.785742Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-07-03T16:52:51.073404Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-07-03T16:52:51.071512Z"
    },
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 1.298788,
     "end_time": "2026-07-03T16:52:51.075279+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-07-03T16:52:49.776491+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# Fit with order p=3\n",
    "model_ar = ts.ar(p=3)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Display model summary\n",
    "# print(model_ar.summary())\n",
    "\n",
    "# Plot results\n",
    "# forecast_steps specifies how many steps to forecast into the future\n",
    "model_ar.plot(forecast_steps=50, alpha=0.5)\n",
    "plt.title(\"AR(3) Model Forecast\")\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "## 2. MA (Moving Average) Model\n",
    "\n",
    "The MA model assumes that the current value depends on past prediction errors (white noise).\n",
    "Use the `ts.ma(q)` method."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "fd2c3e20",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-07-03T16:52:51.146581Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-07-03T16:52:51.145968Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-07-03T16:52:51.920966Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-07-03T16:52:51.919945Z"
    },
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 0.790714,
     "end_time": "2026-07-03T16:52:51.924925+00:00",
     "exception": false,

     "status": "completed"

   ],
   "source": [
    "# Fit with order q=3\n",
    "model_ma = ts.ma(q=3)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Plot results\n",
    "model_ma.plot(forecast_steps=50, alpha=0.5)\n",
    "plt.title(\"MA(3) Model Forecast\")\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]

   "source": [
    "## 3. ARMA (AutoRegressive Moving Average) Model\n",
    "\n",
    "The ARMA model combines AR and MA.\n",
    "Use the `ts.arma(p, q)` method."
   ]
  },

   "cell_type": "code",

   "source": [
    "## 4. ARIMA / Auto-ARIMA\n",
    "\n",
    "The ARIMA model removes non-stationarity (such as trends) by differencing, then applies the ARMA model.\n",
    "\n",
    "Use the `ts.arima()` method.\n",
    "With the `auto=True` option, the `pmdarima` library is used to automatically search for optimal parameters (p, d, q). This is the most recommended approach."
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "try:\n",
    "    print(\"Searching for optimal ARIMA parameters... (this may take a few seconds)\")\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Seasonality can also be considered\n",
    "    # m is the number of steps in a seasonal period\n",
    "    model_auto = ts.arima(auto=True, auto_kwargs={\"seasonal\": True, \"m\": 50})\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Show info of the optimal model found\n",
    "    print(model_auto.summary())\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Plot results (Forecasting for a longer period)\n",
    "    ax = model_auto.plot(forecast_steps=100, alpha=0.5)\n",
    "    plt.title(\"Auto-ARIMA Model Forecast (Seasonal)\")\n",
    "    plt.show()\n",
    "except ImportError as e:\n",
    "    print(f\"Auto-ARIMA skipping: {e}\")\n"
   ]

    "if \"model_auto\" not in dir():\n",
    "    print(\"Auto-ARIMA model not available (pmdarima may be missing); skipping forecast.\")\n",
    "else:\n",

    "\n",
    "    # Get forecast values and confidence intervals\n",
    "    forecast_ts, intervals = model_auto.forecast(\n",

    "    )  # 50% confidence interval\n",
    "\n",
    "    print(\"Forecast Data:\")\n",
    "    print(forecast_ts)\n",
    "\n",
    "    print(\"\\nConfidence Interval (Upper):\")\n",
    "    print(intervals[\"upper\"])\n",

   "source": [
    "## 6. Application in Gravitational Wave Data Analysis: Noise Removal (Whitening) with ARIMA\n",
    "\n",
    "In gravitational wave data analysis, a process called **whitening** is performed to extract burst signals or ringdown waveforms from stationary \"colored noise\".\n",
    "By training an ARIMA model as a predictive model for background noise and subtracting the predicted values from the measured values (taking residuals), it is possible to remove noise and enhance the signal."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "89f2ddd1",
   "metadata": {
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 0.008906,
     "end_time": "2026-07-03T17:09:33.988476+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-07-03T17:09:33.979570+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": [
     "lang-en"
    ]
   },
   "source": [
    "### Step 1: Generating Colored Noise and Injecting a Signal\n",
    "First, we create colored noise with strong low-frequency components (AR(1) process), and embed a weak signal (sine-Gaussian) that is difficult to distinguish otherwise.\n",
    "Note: We use \"strain\" as the unit, which is recognizable by Astropy."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 9,
   "id": "1838cce6",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-07-03T17:09:34.028289Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-07-03T17:09:34.028052Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-07-03T17:09:34.193157Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-07-03T17:09:34.192313Z"
    },
    "papermill": {
     "duration": 0.17632,
     "end_time": "2026-07-03T17:09:34.193879+00:00",
     "exception": false,
     "start_time": "2026-07-03T17:09:34.017559+00:00",
     "status": "completed"
    },
    "tags": []
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 1000x400 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "\n",
    "from gwexpy.timeseries import TimeSeries\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def generate_mock_data(duration=10, fs=1024):\n",
    "    t = np.linspace(0, duration, int(duration * fs))\n",
    "\n",
    "    # 1. Background Noise (AR(1) process with strong autocorrelation)\n",
    "    np.random.seed(42)\n",
    "    white_noise = np.random.normal(0, 1, len(t))\n",
    "    colored_noise = np.zeros_like(white_noise)\n",
    "    for i in range(1, len(t)):\n",
    "        colored_noise[i] = 0.95 * colored_noise[i - 1] + white_noise[i]\n",
    "\n",
    "    # 2. Injected Signal (Sine-Gaussian)\n",
    "    center_time = 5.0\n",
    "    sig_freq = 50.0\n",
    "    width = 0.1\n",
    "    signal = (\n",
    "        2.0\n",
    "        * np.exp(-((t - center_time) ** 2) / (2 * width**2))\n",
    "        * np.sin(2 * np.pi * sig_freq * t)\n",
    "    )\n",
    "\n",
    "    data = colored_noise + signal\n",
    "    # Use a standard unit string that astropy/gwpy can recognize\n",
    "    return TimeSeries(data, t0=0, dt=1 / fs, unit=\"strain\", name=\"MockData\")\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "ts = generate_mock_data()\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.figure(figsize=(10, 4))\n",
    "plt.plot(ts, color=\"gray\")\n",
    "plt.title(\"Original Noisy Data (Signal is hidden here)\")\n",
    "plt.xlabel(\"Time [s]\")\n",
    "plt.grid(True, linestyle=\":\")\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {

   "id": "538002fe",

   "source": [
    "### Step 2: Noise Modeling with ARIMA\n",
    "Using `auto=True`, we search for the optimal model that expresses the autocorrelation structure of the background noise."
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "print(\"Searching for optimal noise model parameters...\")\n",
    "# We prioritize AR model for whitening, so we set max_p=5 and max_q=0.\n",
    "model = ts.arima(auto=True, max_p=5, max_q=0)\n",
    "print(f\"Best model order: {model.res.model.order}\")\n",
    "print(model.summary())"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "### Step 3: Extracting and Visualizing Residuals\n",
    "By subtracting the \"stationary noise\" predicted by the model, we obtain the residuals $x_r = x - \\hat{x}$. This is the whitened data."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 11,
   "id": "d543880e",

   "source": [
    "ts_whitened = model.residuals()\n",
    "ts_whitened.name = \"Whitened Data\"\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 8), sharex=True)\n",
    "\n",
    "ax[0].plot(ts, color=\"gray\", alpha=0.5, label=\"Original\")\n",
    "ax[0].set_title(\"Original Noisy Data\")\n",
    "ax[0].legend(loc=\"upper right\")\n",
    "\n",
    "ax[1].plot(ts_whitened, color=\"red\", label=\"Residuals (Whitened)\")\n",
    "ax[1].set_title(\"Whitened Data (Signal is now visible!)\")\n",
    "ax[1].axvspan(4.8, 5.2, color=\"orange\", alpha=0.3, label=\"Injected Signal Position\")\n",
    "ax[1].legend(loc=\"upper right\")\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },

    "We calculate and compare the Power Spectral Density (PSD)."

  },

   "source": [
    "fft_original = ts.psd()\n",
    "fft_whitened = ts_whitened.psd()\n",
    "\n",
    "plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))\n",
    "plt.loglog(\n",

    "plt.loglog(\n",

    "    alpha=0.7,\n",
    ")\n",
    "plt.title(\"PSD Comparison: Effect of ARIMA Whitening\")\n",
    "plt.xlabel(\"Frequency [Hz]\")\n",
    "plt.ylabel(\"PSD [1/Hz]\")\n",
    "plt.legend()\n",
    "plt.grid(True, which=\"both\", linestyle=\":\")\n",
    "plt.show()"

   "source": [
    "### Summary\n",
    "- Using `model.residuals()`, whitening can be easily performed without writing complex mathematical formulas.\n",
    "- This technique is very powerful for searching for burst signals in gravitational wave analysis and for extracting ringdown waveforms (exponentially decaying sinusoids) immediately after events.\n",
    "\n",
    "- **Related API**: [Time Series API](../../reference/api/timeseries.rst)\n",
    "- **Related theory**: [Validated Algorithms](../validated_algorithms.md), [Numerical Stability](../numerical_stability.md)"
   ]
  }
